In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the regional differences in excitatory and inhibtitory amino acid-induced current responses are not due to the regional differences in the receptor density, but to the differences in the size of the neurons.

the Glu, GABA, Asp and Gly receptors are distributed in a homogeneous manner, and the regional variation of the current density of the responses is due to the difference of the cell size of respective CNS regions.

the regional heterogeneity of the excitatory amino acid response is not observed when the response is expressed in terms of current amplitude, but is observed when it is expressed in terms terms of current density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regional differences in the excitatory amino acid-induced responses are due to regional heterogeneity in the number of receptors per unit surface area of the neurons, whereas that in the inhibitory amino acid responses is mainly due to regional heterogeneities in the number of channels per unit surface area.
the regional differences of excitatory amino acid responses are due to the differences in neuronal size and/or membrane surface area rather than the regional differences of amino acid receptors.

the regional heterogeneity of excitatory and/or inhibitory amino acid responses in CNS neurons may be due to the regional differences in the number of amino acid receptors, the density of the amino acid receptors, or the regional differences in neuronal membrane surface area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are regional differences in the excitatory amino acid responses of CNS neurons, and these regional variations are not due to the differences in the facilitation by Gly.
the regional differences in the amino acid-induced responses are not due to the differences in amino acid receptors but to the differences in neuronal membrane areas.
the regional heterogeneity of the responses to excitatory amino acids and glycine in the CNS may be due to regional variation in the density of their receptors.
